newsitem.title: USA: U.S. term limit backers say will focus on states.
newsitem.headline: U.S. term limit backers say will focus on states.

text.p: Supporters of limiting the terms of members of Congress acknowledged Tuesday they had an uphill fight in Washington this year and said they would focus their efforts on raising support at the state level.

Paul Jacob, executive director of U.S. Term Limits, which seeks to limit congressional terms, said the House leadership did not appear interested in promoting the issue, while Senate Republican leader Trent Lott of Mississippi opposed it.
"Our primary focus is at the state level," Jacob told a news conference.

"I'm not going to say we're going to spend all our resources and energy lobbying Congress because it would be a much more effective strategy to go directly to the voters and show them a way they can really up the pressure on Congress," Jacob said.

He said his group's strategy was to push for states to pass laws that instruct their elected members of Congress to support term limits and provide voters with the information on whether the members have followed those instructions.
Jacob said nine states already have these laws, called "informed voter laws," and he predicted another dozen states would pass them by next year, including California, Michigan, Ohio and Florida.

Last year a filibuster ended Senate consideration of a proposed constitutional amendment that would have limited members of Congress to 12 years in office. Senators Fred Thompson of Tennessee and John Ashcroft of Missouri have said they intend to re-introduce the proposal this year.
The same amendment failed to pass the House in 1995 despite polls showing that up to three-quarters of Americans favor term limits.
